content.text: [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-products-africa-minimum-viable-stack-actually|selling]] a digital product should be a simple transaction. You build something valuable — an ebook, a course, a Notion template, a font family, a preset pack, a beat — and someone pays you for access to it. The file transfers. The transaction completes. But for millions of creators, the [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-options-ethiopian-digital-creators-honest-side-side|COREMERCH guide to payment]] layer is where [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/everything-you-need-know-about-automated-digital-product-2|Everything You]] breaks down. Stripe is unavailable. PayPal flags the account. Gumroad holds the payout. The workarounds stop working. What actually works is a sovereign commerce stack: a static storefront on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, automatic payment verification through NOWPayments, and delivery triggered by a webhook the moment the transaction confirms on-chain. No platform intermediary. No payout schedule. No geography filter. The customer owns the storefront code, the order history, the customer list, and the product files. COREMERCH has no access after deployment.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/everything-you-need-know-about-automated-digital-product-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.
content.title: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments

content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Payment gateway

The automated delivery pipeline for digital products follows a specific sequence that eliminates every manual step. A buyer visits the storefront, selects a product, and initiates payment. The checkout displays a QR code with the exact wallet address and payment amount in their chosen cryptocurrency, converted from USD at the current exchange rate via live price feeds. The buyer sends the payment from their wallet. NOWPayments monitors the blockchain and detects the incoming transaction within seconds of broadcast. When the transaction receives sufficient confirmations on-chain, NOWPayments fires a webhook to your Cloudflare Worker or Google Apps Script endpoint. The backend verifies the payment amount, confirms the transaction hash on the blockchain directly, logs the order, generates a receipt, and sends the download link to the buyer's email address.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

Pricing digital products in crypto is straightforward because NOWPayments handles the currency conversion automatically. You set your price in USD. The checkout pulls live exchange rates and displays the exact amount in whichever cryptocurrency the buyer selects. For USDT-denominated products, there is no conversion at all — one dollar in equals one dollar received, minus network fees that typically amount to less than $0.10 on Tron or Solana. You receive the crypto equivalent of your USD price in the wallet you configured in your NOWPayments account. COREMERCH never touches these funds at any point — the wallet is yours from the moment of setup and remains yours unconditionally.
Who This Is Built For and Why

The product types that work with automated crypto delivery are any digital files that can be stored and delivered via download link: ebooks in PDF or EPUB format, courses packaged as ZIP archives, Notion templates exported as files or share links, font families as ZIP archives of OTF and TTF files, Lightroom or Capture One preset packs, beat files as WAV or MP3 archives, plugin installers, stock photo packs, software license keys, and any other file-based product. The delivery system in Stack 01 uses Google Drive shared links. Stack 02 uses Cloudflare R2 presigned URLs with configurable expiry times — typically 24 to 72 hours — which prevents download links from being shared indefinitely after a single purchase.
Sovereign digital commerce stacks empower digital sellers to take control of their financial freedom.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The key components of the sovereign digital commerce stack include GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. NOWPayments integrates with this architecture to handle automatic on-chain cryptocurrency payment verification, making it possible for digital sellers to process cryptocurrency payments in USD, converted at transaction time.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

Digital sellers can deploy their sovereign digital commerce stack today by using the Complete Builder Kit ($197), which includes all 6 blueprints and 7 templates for instant deployment and scaling. They can also purchase individual components, such as the Sovereign Starter Stack ($97), to build and deploy their stack. Additionally, they can visit the Shop at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html to explore more options.
How do I sell an ebook online without PayPal or Stripe?

The fastest path to your first sovereign digital product sale is a three-step process. First, create a NOWPayments account — configure your wallet addresses for USDT on Tron and Bitcoin as starting points, generate your API key, and set the webhook endpoint URL. Second, choose your stack: Stack 01 uses GitHub Pages plus Google Apps Script and takes most creators four to six hours following the Sovereign Blueprint at $47; Stack 02 uses Cloudflare Pages plus Workers plus Supabase and is deployed by COREMERCH in 48 hours with the Edge Commerce Stack at $197. Third, upload your product files, set your prices in USD, and run a complete mainnet test transaction before promoting.
With NOWPayments, digital sellers can process cryptocurrency payments in USD, converted at transaction time.

Digital sellers in restricted regions, such as Zimbabwe, can leverage the Complete Builder Kit ($197) to deploy and scale their sovereign digital commerce stack. Additionally, they can explore more options at the Shop at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html. This solution enables financial freedom and infrastructure sovereignty, making it possible to sell digital products without relying on international payment processors like Stripe or PayPal.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your sovereign digital commerce stack today, follow these steps: purchase the Complete Builder Kit ($197) or individual components, such as the Sovereign Starter Stack ($97); deploy your stack using GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting and Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic; integrate NOWPayments for automatic on-chain cryptocurrency payment verification; configure order storage using Supabase or Google Sheets and file delivery using Google Drive or Cloudflare R2; and test your stack for end-to-end functionality.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the fee difference between Gumroad and NOWPayments?
At 100 sales per month on a $97 product, Gumroad's 10% commission translates to $921, while NOWPayments charges just 0.5%.
Can I use multiple cryptocurrencies with NOWPayments?
Yes, NOWPayments supports over 300 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, and charges a 0.5% fee only.
How do I configure order storage using Supabase or Google Sheets?
You can configure order storage by integrating Supabase or Google Sheets with your sovereign digital commerce stack, following the instructions provided in the Complete Builder Kit ($197).
What is the benefit of using a sovereign digital commerce stack?

A sovereign digital commerce stack enables infrastructure sovereignty and financial freedom, allowing you to sell digital products without relying on international payment processors like Stripe or PayPal, and avoiding costly platform fees.
Can I use a sovereign digital commerce stack to sell physical products?
No, a sovereign digital commerce stack is designed for digital products only, but you can use it to sell physical products via dropshipping or other fulfillment methods.
